To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the single transverse-spin asymmetry of the pion production in semi‐inclusive deep‐inelastic scattering (SIDIS) can be understood in terms of the quark‐spin‐orbit interaction, which is the same interaction that is responsible for the spin‐orbit interaction of electrons in the atom.

the single spin asymmetries are sensitive to the quark orbital motion of the nucleon, which is a consequence of the chiral anomaly, and that the single spin and double spin asymmetries can be used to measure the orbital angular momentum of quarks in a nucleon, and to determine the sign of the orbital angular momentum.

the single‐transverse‐spin‐dependent asymmetries in the semi‐inclusive deep inelastic scattering process are related to the quark orbital angular momentum (OAM) of the nucleon, and that the quark OAM is a non‐trivial function of Bjorken x.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spin structure of nucleons and nuclei.
the single transverse-spin asymmetry (SSA) in the semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) and the proton-proton scattering.
the study of the spin structure of the nucleon, which is one of the most important and challenging problems in hadron physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quark‐angular‐momentums in the nucleon are very important for the single spin asymmetry, but not the only factor.
the single spin asymmetries are not a direct probe of the orbital angular momentum of the quarks, and the orbital motion of the quarks is not a direct source of the single spin asymmetry.
the quark‐angular‐momenta in the nucleon are indeed important for the understanding of the single transverse asymmetry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the quark‐spin and quark‐orb‐ang‐mom of nucleon are related to the single transverse asymmetry of the Drell‐Yan process, the SIDIS, and the pion production process in the proton‐nucleus scattering, respectively.
the single transverse-spin asymmetry in the semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering is related to the quark orbital angular momentum in the nucleon.

the single transverse asymmetry can be understood as a consequence of the orbital motion of quarks in the nucleon, and the transverse momentum of the quark is a result of the interaction between the nucleon and the target.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the single spin asymmetries in the semi‐inclusive deep‐inelastic scattering process are sensitive to the quark orbital motion in the nucleon and can provide a new way to study the quark orbital motions in the nucleon.
the transverse single spin asymmetry is a consequence of the quark‐orbit angular momentum.
the transverse single spin asymmetry is related to the difference in quark orbital angular momentum between the proton and antiproton.
